A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REALM framework. Their complete main texts and appendices A-C are readable, and equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original TREC evaluations, component ablations, initial-order sensitivity experiments and pairwise model-capability results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds BEIR evaluations, RankGPT comparisons, a hyperparameter sweep and inference-iteration measurements.

M1.justification: Gaussian relevance modeling, probabilistic TrueSkill updates, recursive pruning and pivot optimizations are retained. Section 3.3 newly specifies a median-score initial pivot when uncertainties tie, filling an implementation gap without establishing a change to the previously implemented procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates TREC DL 2019 and 2020. V2 adds Covid, SciFact, DBpedia and NFCorpus from BEIR, substantially extending coverage beyond general web search to biomedical, scientific fact-verification, entity-centric and consumer-health retrieval domains.

E2.justification: RankGPT, previously discussed but not evaluated, is added in Appendix C.1/Table 5 for both TREC datasets and three Flan-T5 sizes. The original four LLM baselines and BM25 remain; the BEIR experiments reuse that original comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a controlled lambda sweep over 0, 1/3, 2/3 and 1 on TREC DL 2020 and adds mean refinement iterations as an efficiency measure. Existing TREC query counts, BM25 top-100 candidates, top-10 evaluation, model configurations and default lambda = 2/3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds sensitivity analysis of the partition-mixing parameter, and Appendix C.3/Table 7 examines recursive iteration requirements. These focused additions supplement the retained component ablations, initial-order robustness test and pairwise model-capability analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 in both versions reports dataset-averaged scores from a single run. V2 adds no seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Its new iteration counts describe inference rounds, not experimental replications.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 1-4 retain their numerical contents as v2 Tables 1, 3, 4 and 6. Substantial new results include REALM's BEIR NDCG@10 scores of 78.4, 69.3, 45.9 and 36.4 with Flan-T5-Large, RankGPT scores, lambda sensitivity and an overall mean of 4.89 iterations. These extend the evidence rather than improve previously reported TREC scores.

T1.justification: The preference-probability formula, natural-parameter updates, pivot aggregation, partition formula and complexity statements are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same Bayesian-rating exposition and update equations; no proof or mathematical correction is added.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and claims of improved ranking quality, stability and efficiency remain unchanged. V2's abstract adds numerical improvement ranges already reported in v1 Section 4.2; the introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 replaces a generic future-work sentence with a specific limitation concerning untested skew-normal relevance distributions and their potential costs. It also interprets the lambda sweep as a quality-cost tradeoff, iteration counts as supporting potential parallelization, and RankGPT failures as consequences of model context limitations.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the initial pivot tie-breaking rule, adds a source-code repository link in Appendix B.4 and reports iPapers integration in a title footnote. Existing hardware, baseline hyperparameters and substantive prompt instructions are retained. The PDFs establish these added disclosures, not independent verification of the linked resources.

R1.justification: V2 adds the BEIR citation to Thakur et al. and removes Fukuda and Tomiura's academic-search citation and accompanying discussion. The related-work taxonomy and REALM's positioning remain largely unchanged. MS MARCO attribution and publication-metadata updates refer to retained works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized introduction and language edits, adds quantitative detail to the abstract, revises the author/contact block and adds acknowledgments and several experimental or appendix subsections. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands visual reporting with the multi-domain BEIR table, a two-panel lambda-sensitivity figure, and RankGPT and iteration tables. Existing tables are relocated and renumbered, while Figures 1-2 retain their content. The principal change is added visual evidence rather than numerical edits to existing displays.

improvement.justification: V1's benchmark evidence was confined to two TREC collections built on MS MARCO. V2's four BEIR datasets substantially strengthen evidence for applicability across retrieval domains. The sensitivity study better supports the existing default, while the pivot clarification and code link improve reproducibility documentation. BEIR testing remains limited to Flan-T5-Large and results remain single-run, but the additions address a substantial gap in empirical generality.
